newsitem.title: USA: AES restructures GPU power sale.
newsitem.headline: AES restructures GPU power sale.

text.p: AES Corp said Tuesday it has executed three restructured power purchase agreements for an aggregate 520 megawatts with GPU Energy, the energy services and delivery business of GPU Inc.
AES said it plans to build a 720 megawatt natural gas-fired, combined cycle facility, named AES Ironwood, in Southeastern Pennsylvania to service these contracts.

In 1996, AES noted, it acquired the rights to the three power purchase agreements from other suppliers for a total cost of $28 million. AES and GPU Energy are now working together to finalize a site for the plant.
The agreement is subject to approval by the Pennsylvania Public Utilities Commission, GPU spokesman Gary Plummer pointed out.
He said it replaces agreements the utility originally had with York City Energy Partners, Blue Mountain Power and Altoona Cogeneration Partners.
The renegotiated contract has an eight year term with options for extentions, Plummer said.
AES spokesman Kenneth Woodcock said the plant is expected to cost $400 per kilowatt -- a total of some $300 million, to be funded with non-recourse, project financing.
The debt will probably go to market next year, once the plant's site and technology have been selected, he said.
The power plant is expected to complete construction and begin commercial operations in the year 2000, AES said.
Woodcock said the price of the power will be based on a tolling charge, with GPU providing the natural gas.
This is expected to result in electricity costs in the $0.03 per kilowatt hour range, Woodcock said.
The "planned facility is one of the largest independent power plants to be built in the U.S. in the 1990's," AES said.
It said the continuing joint effort by AES and GPU Energy should result in a unique project that sets a precedent for the U.S. market.
AES also John H. McArthur, former dean of the Harvard Business School, was appointed to its board.
In addition, John Ruggirello, the division director of AES Enterprise, which serves most of the United States market, was named a vice president of the corporation.

Furthermore, AES created a new division that will be responsible for AES's electricity supply business in parts of Asia and the Middle East as well as some of the countries that were formerly a part of the U.S.S.R.

Paul Stinson, who is currently the plant manager of AES's Medway facility in England, was named the division director and Shazad Quazim, who initiated AES's business in Pakistan, will join the new division.
